Lu Qi resented Zhang Yi's great reputation and upright conduct and had no means to entrap him. As troops were then being deployed on the western frontier, Qi falsely offered to go in person. The emperor firmly refused, and instead recommended Zhang Yi, with the title of vice director of the Secretariat, as military governor of Fengxiang-Longyou to replace Zhu Ci. Zhang Yi then entered into an alliance with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others at Qingshui.

Lu Qi resented Zhang Yi's great reputation and upright conduct and had no means to entrap him. As troops were then being deployed on the western frontier, Qi falsely offered to go in person. The emperor firmly refused, and Qi therefore recommended Zhang Yi, with the title of vice director of the Secretariat, as military governor of Fengxiang-Longyou to replace Zhu Ci. Zhang Yi then entered into an alliance with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others at Qingshui.
After 杞乃偽請行 and 上固以不可, 因薦鎰 continues Lu Qi’s scheme: Qi, not the emperor, recommended Zhang Yi for the Fengxiang-Longyou posting.

At first it was agreed that Han would use an ox and Tibet a horse as sacrificial victims; Yi was ashamed to ally with them and, intending to diminish the rite, therefore requested of Jiezan, saying: 'Han cannot plow without oxen, and Tibet cannot travel without horses—now I request that sheep, pigs, and dogs be substituted for the three animals.'

At first it was agreed that Han would use an ox and Tibet a horse as sacrificial victims; Yi was ashamed to ally with them and, intending to diminish the rite, therefore requested of Jiezan, saying: 'Han cannot plow without oxen, and Tibet cannot travel without horses—now I request that the three animals sheep, pigs, and dogs be substituted for them.'
以羊豕犬三物代之 makes sheep, pigs, and dogs the three substitutes for the ox and horse; ‘for the three animals’ wrongly treats 三物 as the things replaced.
When Zhang Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, his two sons were seized by scouting cavalry, and Li Chulin had them all killed;
When Zhang Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, he and his two sons were all seized by scouting cavalry, and Li Chulin killed them all;
鎰出鳳翔三十里，及二子皆為候騎所得 coordinates Zhang Yi with his two sons as those captured; 楚琳俱殺之 and the following 贈太子太傅 show he was killed too.
When Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, his two sons were both seized by scouting cavalry, and Chulin killed them all;
When Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, he and his two sons were all seized by scouting cavalry, and Chulin killed them all;
The literal likewise omits 鎰 from 及二子皆為候騎所得 and from 俱殺之; he and the two sons were jointly taken and killed.

Lin Fu's son Xiangdao served as right chief minister at the beginning of the Linde era; Xiangdao was Congyi's great-granduncle.
麟德 is the Linde reign, not Longde; 曾伯祖 is a paternal great-granduncle, not a great-great-uncle.

Fu replied, "I am selling my old estate because my family is poor, intending only to rescue widows and children. If I exchanged it for a fine post for myself and left those within my gates to freeze and starve, that would not be the heart of a base man."
非鄙夫之心也 is ‘not the heart of a base/petty man’; rendering 鄙夫 as ‘honorable man’ inverts Fu’s refusal.
